proofs.full_local_argument: Write C=C_f and h_t=f(x_t)-f(x*). Compactness and continuity give a minimizer x*. Each LMO exists because its objective is continuous on nonempty compact D. Since gamma_t=2/(t+2) belongs to (0,1], induction using convexity of D gives x_t in D for all t. Define g_t=<x_t-s_t,grad f(x_t)>. Convexity gives h_t<=<grad f(x_t),x_t-x*>. Exact minimization gives <s_t,grad f(x_t)><=<x*,grad f(x_t)>, hence h_t<=g_t. By the definition of curvature at x_t,s_t and gamma_t, f(x_{t+1})<=f(x_t)-gamma_t g_t+(gamma_t^2/2)C. Therefore h_{t+1}<=(1-gamma_t)h_t+(gamma_t^2/2)C. At t=0, gamma_0=1, so h_1<=C/2<=2C/3. Suppose t>=1 and h_t<=2C/(t+2). Substitution yields h_{t+1}<=2C(t+1)/(t+2)^2. Since (t+1)(t+3)=(t+2)^2-1<=(t+2)^2, this is <=2C/(t+3), completing induction. Every denominator is positive and every multiplication uses C>=0, so C=0 is included; then h_k=0 for k>=1 because h_k>=0. The proof used no restriction on tie choices, and is therefore pointwise for every exact selection sequence. No duality-gap convergence theorem or external unreviewed lead is needed.

assumptions: D is nonempty, compact and convex; finite dimension n>=1.
f is convex and continuously differentiable as stated, with finite C_f>=0.
Every gradient and linear minimizer is exact; the step size is exactly 2/(t+2).
statement.conclusion: The iterate is feasible and f(x_k)-f(x*)<=2C_f/(k+2). The conclusion concerns the final iterate's primal error, not a last-iterate duality-gap bound or a lower bound for arbitrary algorithms.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let n>=1 and D be a nonempty compact convex subset of R^n with its Euclidean inner product. Let f be real-valued, convex and continuously differentiable on an open neighborhood of D. Set C_f=sup_{x,s in D, 0<gamma<=1} (2/gamma^2)[f(x+gamma(s-x))-f(x)-gamma<grad f(x),s-x>]. Let x* be any minimizer over D. Starting at x_0 in D, choose s_t in argmin_{s in D}<s,grad f(x_t)> and set x_{t+1}=(1-2/(t+2))x_t+(2/(t+2))s_t for t>=0.
statement.parameter_domains: n is an integer >=1; k is an integer >=1; 0<=C_f<infinity. This is the delta=0 case only. Positive epsilon is needed only for a derived stopping-budget interpretation.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such instance, every feasible x_0, every sequence of exact LMO minimizers and every integer k>=1, the conclusion holds. There is no probabilistic qualifier. Arbitrary tie choices, including randomized choices, satisfy the same pathwise bound.
